az.lead: Your first own flat, step by step. Tap an area.
az.notiz.t: For example dates, names or what you still want to ask. Stays only on this device.
az.speicherFehler: Saving did not work. Your ticks may be lost when you close the app.
az.u25.warn.h: Under 25 and receiving Grundsicherungsgeld? Ask first, then sign!
az.u25.warn: Are you under 25 and do you (or your family) receive Grundsicherungsgeld from the Jobcenter – or will you need it after the move? Then get the Jobcenter's approval (Zusicherung) BEFORE you sign the rental contract. Otherwise, until you are 25, the Jobcenter often pays no rent and no first furnishing (§ 22 Abs. 5 SGB II).
az.brief.kopiert: Copied. Paste the text into an email or a document.
az.brief.hinweis: The letter is in German because the Jugendamt needs it that way. Fill in the gaps. If you already had help from a Jugendamt before, the letter usually goes to that Jugendamt – even if you have moved (§ 86a Abs. 4 SGB VIII). Otherwise to the Jugendamt where you live. Hand it in and have them confirm receipt on a copy.
az.brief.label: Letter (you can edit it here)
az.vers.tipp: No advertising, no providers: compare prices and conditions yourself. Independent advice is available at the consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) – usually for a fee, often reduced.
az.stand: Legal status: {d}. These notes do not replace advice.
az.vers.t: What you need – and what you don't
az.hilfen.t: What you may be entitled to
az.care.t: From a residential group, care home or foster family
az.p.leisten: Work out what you can afford
az.p.leisten.t:
Write down what you get every month and what you have to pay: rent including heating and service charges, electricity, phone, food, travel ticket, insurance. What is left is your money to live on.
Also plan something for the unexpected, for example an extra payment.
az.p.u25: Under 25 with Grundsicherungsgeld: approval before signing
az.p.u25.t:
Ask the Jobcenter in writing before you sign the rental contract. Without approval (Zusicherung), until you are 25 the Jobcenter often pays no rent, no heating and no first furnishing. And you get less money to live on (§ 20 Abs. 3 SGB II).
The Jobcenter must approve if you cannot live with your parents for serious social reasons, if the flat is needed for work, or for a similarly important reason (§ 22 Abs. 5 SGB II, § 24 Abs. 6 SGB II). If you come from youth welfare (Jugendhilfe), write this in your application to the Jobcenter.
Already signed? Go to the Jobcenter straight away anyway. If you could not wait for an important reason, it can do without the approval.
az.p.suche: Look for a flat – and think of the housing entitlement certificate
az.p.suche.t:
With a housing entitlement certificate (Wohnberechtigungsschein, WBS) you can rent a cheaper social housing flat. People with a low income get it from the town or municipality.
Halls of residence for trainees or students and shared flats (WG) are often cheaper too.
az.p.vertrag.t:
Look at the basic rent (Kaltmiete), the service charges (Nebenkosten, Betriebskosten) and heating. Together this is the total rent (Warmmiete).
The deposit (Kaution) may be at most 3 months' basic rent. You may pay it in 3 monthly instalments, the first at the start of the tenancy (§ 551 BGB).
Do not sign anything under pressure. Ask if you don't understand something.
az.p.uebergabe: At the handover: record and photos
az.p.uebergabe.t:
Walk through the flat with the landlord. Write down all damage (Übergabeprotokoll) and take photos. Note the meter readings for electricity, gas and water.
Both of you sign; you get a copy. Then you will not have to pay for old damage later.
az.p.erstausstattung: Apply for first furnishing – before you buy
az.p.erstausstattung.t:
Do you receive Grundsicherungsgeld from the Jobcenter? Then you can get money or items for your first furnishing, including household appliances such as a cooker or fridge (Erstausstattung, § 24 Abs. 3 SGB II).
Apply before you buy: the Jobcenter does not pay for the time before the application (§ 37 SGB II). Under 25 only with approval (Zusicherung).
az.p.kaution: Deposit: possible as a loan from the Jobcenter
az.p.kaution.t:
If you receive Grundsicherungsgeld, the Jobcenter at your new place can cover the deposit – usually as a loan that you pay back later. This only works with approval in advance.
Moving costs can also be covered if your previous Jobcenter agrees in advance (§ 22 Abs. 6 SGB II).
az.p.wg: Shared flat: main tenant or subtenant?
az.p.wg.t:
If your name is on the rental contract (main tenant, Hauptmieter), you have all the rights and duties of the contract.
If you rent a room from a flatmate (subtenant, Untermieter), that flatmate is your contract partner. They need the landlord's permission (§ 540 BGB). Ask to see it and make a written subletting contract.
az.p.schufaAuskunft: Schufa report: use the free copy of your data
az.p.schufaAuskunft.t:
Landlords often want a Schufa report. You get a copy of your data free of charge (Datenkopie, Art. 15 DSGVO). You do not need paid offers for this.
If you have rented before, landlords often ask for confirmation from your old landlord that you have no rent debts (Mietschuldenfreiheitsbescheinigung).
az.p.melden.t:
Register at the citizens' office (Bürgeramt, Meldebehörde) within 2 weeks of moving in (§ 17 BMG). Many towns offer appointments online.
Take your ID and the landlord's confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). Your landlord must give it to you (§ 19 BMG).
az.p.strom: Sign up for electricity and note the meter reading
az.p.strom.t:
Sign an electricity contract. On the day you move in, note the meter reading and take a photo.
Without your own contract you get electricity from the default supplier (Grundversorger). Then you must tell them (§ 2 StromGVV). Compare prices.
Set the monthly advance payment realistically. Otherwise a large extra payment comes at the end of the year.
az.p.rundfunk: Register for the broadcasting fee – or apply for exemption
az.p.rundfunk.t:
Only one fee is paid per flat. In a shared flat one person registers; the others do not pay twice. Share the fee among yourselves.
Exemption is possible with Grundsicherungsgeld or social assistance – and with BAföG, vocational training allowance (Berufsausbildungsbeihilfe) or training allowance (Ausbildungsgeld) if you do not live with your parents (§ 4 Abs. 1 RBeitrStV). Exemption is only granted on application with proof. In a shared flat it only applies to you: if a flatmate is not exempt, they pay the fee.
az.p.haftpflicht.t: Personal liability insurance (Privathaftpflicht) pays if you accidentally damage something of someone else's. You are often covered by your parents' policy while you are at school or doing your first training. At the latest after that you need your own.
az.p.adresse.t:
Bank, health insurance, employer or school and university, Familienkasse (Kindergeld), Jobcenter and other offices, insurance, phone contract.
Anyone receiving benefits must report changes immediately (§ 60 SGB I).
az.p.internet: Internet and phone: watch the contract term
az.p.internet.t: Compare prices. A new contract may run for at most 24 months. After that you can cancel at any time with one month's notice (§ 56 TKG).
az.p.post.t:
With a forwarding order (Nachsendeauftrag) at the post office, letters to your old address reach you for some time. This costs money.
Put your name on the doorbell and letterbox.
az.p.papiere.t:
ID, birth certificate, school certificates, health insurance card, rental contract, tax identification number (Steuer-ID) and pension insurance number (Sozialversicherungsausweis).
For training or a job, your employer needs your Steuer-ID and date of birth (§ 39e Abs. 4 EStG) and your pension insurance number. You can request your Steuer-ID again from the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern).
az.p.arzt.t:
Find a family doctor's practice in your new town.
Emergency (ambulance, fire brigade): 112. Police: 110. Medical on-call service when it is not an emergency and the practice is closed: 116 117.
az.p.haus.t:
Read the house rules, for example about quiet times and the stairwell.
Sort your rubbish the way it is done where you live. This is in the waste calendar of your town or district.
az.p.kfz: Car or motorbike? Report your address
az.p.kfz.t: You must report your new address immediately (unverzüglich) to the vehicle registration office (§ 15 FZV).
az.p.konten.t:
A current account (Girokonto) for wages, rent and shopping. Everyone has the right to a basic account (Basiskonto), even without a fixed address. The bank must offer it within 10 business days at the latest (§ 31 ZKG).
You only need a garnishment protection account (P-Konto) if your account is seized. Any current account can be converted (§ 850k ZPO).
Put something aside every month for emergencies, ideally in an instant access savings account (Tagesgeldkonto).
az.p.trick.t: Set up standing orders that go out shortly after your money arrives: rent, electricity, phone, insurance, savings. What is left is your money to live on for the month.
az.p.vers.t: Essential: health insurance (compulsory) and personal liability insurance. Many other policies are usually unnecessary. The overview shows you what matters.
az.p.termine: Important dates in the month and bank statements
az.p.termine.t:
Note: when does your money arrive? When do rent, electricity and phone go out?
Check your account once a week, also for debits you don't recognise. You can get a direct debit back from your bank up to 8 weeks after it was taken (§ 675x BGB).
az.p.nebenkosten.t:
Once a year the landlord settles the service charges. You must receive it at the latest 12 months after the end of the billing period (§ 556 Abs. 3 BGB). If it comes later, you usually do not have to pay anything extra. If something is wrong, you have 12 months to object.
If you receive Grundsicherungsgeld, hand in an extra payment to the Jobcenter straight away.
az.p.ordner.t:
One folder is enough to start, with sections: flat, work or training, offices, insurance, bank, health.
How long to keep (recommendation of the Verbraucherzentrale): bank statements at least 3 years. Receipts and guarantees 2 years. Rental contract, handover record, service charge statements and deposit until 3 years after moving out. Employment contracts, wage tax certificates and social insurance notifications until retirement. School and work certificates forever.
az.p.raten: No instalment purchases, no “buy now, pay later”
az.p.raten.t: “Pay later” is basically a loan. If you miss a deadline, fees are added. It is easy to lose track.
az.p.dispo: No overdraft as a permanent solution
az.p.dispo.t: An overdraft (Dispo, minus on your account) is expensive. If you are in the minus for 6 months in a row and on average by more than 75 % of your limit, the bank must offer you advice (§ 504a BGB). Get help early, for example from a debt counselling service (Schuldnerberatung).
az.p.handy: Phone contract with an expensive device
az.p.handy.t: You pay off the “cheap” phone through the monthly fee. Add everything up: device and contract over the whole term. A contract without a device is often cheaper.
az.p.ohneSchufa.t: Serious loans are practically never given without a check. Never pay fees in advance: it does not increase your chance of a loan. Get help from a debt counselling service instead.
az.p.abo: Subscription traps and contracts at the door or on the phone
az.p.abo.t:
Don't sign anything straight away. Contracts made at the door, on the phone or online can usually be withdrawn within 14 days (§ 312g and § 355 BGB). Send the withdrawal by email or letter.
Online, the button must clearly say that it costs money, for example “zahlungspflichtig bestellen” (order with obligation to pay) (§ 312j BGB).
az.p.unnoetig.t: Insurance for phones and devices, glass, travel luggage or payment protection insurance for a loan (Restschuldversicherung) is usually unnecessary. What matters is personal liability insurance and health insurance.
az.p.schufa.t:
Schufa collects data on whether you pay bills and loans. Landlords, banks and phone providers ask there. Unpaid bills can lead to a bad entry.
You can find out for free what is stored about you (Datenkopie, Art. 15 DSGVO).
az.p.postLiegen.t: Open letters straight away, especially from offices, courts and debt collectors. Many have deadlines. Against a decision from an office, for example, you usually have one month to object (Widerspruch) (§ 84 SGG).
az.p.bab.t: For in-company training if you do not live with your parents. From 18 also if the company is close to your parents (§ 56, § 60 SGB III). You apply at the employment agency (Agentur für Arbeit).
az.p.bafoeg.t: For university studies and certain schools (§ 2 BAföG). You apply at the education support office (Amt für Ausbildungsförderung), for studies usually via the student services (Studierendenwerk).
az.p.wohngeld.t: A rent subsidy for people with a low income. Note: if you are in training or studies for which there can be BAföG or vocational training allowance, on your own you usually do not get Wohngeld – even if you end up with 0 € funding (§ 20 Abs. 2 WoGG). It can be different if someone lives with you who is not in training, for example your child.
az.p.kindergeld.t:
Up to 18 there is always Kindergeld. Up to 25 in training, studies or voluntary service – also if you are looking for a training place or in a break of up to 4 months. Up to 21 if you are registered as looking for work. After your first training only if you work at most 20 hours a week (§ 32 Abs. 4 EStG).
If your parents pay you no maintenance, you can apply to the Familienkasse to have the Kindergeld paid to you (Abzweigung, § 74 EStG). If your parents have died or you do not know where they are, you can apply for Kindergeld for yourself (§ 1 Abs. 2 BKGG).
az.p.unterhalt.t:
As a rule, your parents must provide for your living costs until your first training is finished. This includes the costs of training (§ 1610 Abs. 2 BGB). How and how much depends on the individual case.
Up to 21, the Jugendamt advises and supports you in claiming maintenance (§ 18 Abs. 4 SGB VIII).
az.p.grundsicherung.t:
If your money is not enough to live on. Under 25: approval (Zusicherung) before moving (§ 22 Abs. 5 SGB II). In addition there may be: first furnishing (§ 24 Abs. 3 SGB II), deposit as a loan and moving costs (§ 22 Abs. 6 SGB II).
Anyone studying or in training for which there can be BAföG or vocational training allowance usually gets no Grundsicherungsgeld, but sometimes allowances (§ 7 Abs. 5, § 27 SGB II).
az.p.rfBefreiung.t: With Grundsicherungsgeld or social assistance. With BAföG, vocational training allowance or training allowance if you do not live with your parents (§ 4 Abs. 1 RBeitrStV). Only on application with proof.
az.p.but.t: Also for young people up to 25 who attend a school – also a vocational school – and get no training pay (§ 28 Abs. 1 SGB II). For example school supplies or tutoring. You need a benefit such as Grundsicherungsgeld, Wohngeld or Kinderzuschlag.
az.p.waisenrente.t: If a parent has died, it is always paid up to 18. During school, training, studies or voluntary service up to 27 (§ 48 Abs. 4 SGB VI). Ask the pension insurance (Rentenversicherung).
az.p.jungVolljaehrig: Help from the Jugendamt also after 18
az.p.jungVolljaehrig.t:
If you can't fully manage on your own yet, you have a right to help for young adults (Hilfe für junge Volljährige, § 41 SGB VIII). You can apply for it yourself at the Jugendamt, ideally early, before your 18th birthday.
It usually lasts until 21, longer in justified cases. If the help has already ended, you can apply again later.
az.p.nachbetreuung.t: The Jugendamt must continue to advise and support you for a while after the help ends (aftercare, Nachbetreuung, § 41a SGB VIII). How long and how much should be written in the care plan (Hilfeplan). The Jugendamt should contact you regularly.
az.p.uebergang.t: The care plan (Hilfeplan) sets out what happens after youth welfare. One year before the planned end, the Jugendamt checks whether another office will then be responsible, for example the Jobcenter or integration assistance (Eingliederungshilfe, help for people with disabilities) (§ 41 Abs. 3, § 36b SGB VIII). Ask what your care plan says.
az.p.kostenbeitrag.t:
You do not have to pay anything to the Jugendamt from your own income, for example training pay or a holiday job (no cost contribution, Kostenbeitrag, § 92 Abs. 1a, § 94 SGB VIII).
Exceptions: if you live in a residential group or foster family and receive Kindergeld yourself, the Jugendamt can claim the Kindergeld as a contribution (§ 94 Abs. 3 SGB VIII). Money paid for the same purpose as the help, for example part of the vocational training allowance, can also be claimed by the Jugendamt (§ 93 Abs. 1 SGB VIII). Ask what applies to you.
az.p.careKv.t:
If you live in a residential group, care home or foster family – also after 18 – the Jugendamt usually covers the costs of illness (Krankenhilfe, § 40, § 41 Abs. 2 SGB VIII).
When the help ends, you need your own health insurance, for example through your training or family insurance (Familienversicherung). Ask early in the care plan meeting and at a health insurance fund.
az.p.beratung: You have a right to advice
az.p.beratung.t:
Get advice, for example at the Jugendamt, a care leaver counselling service or the youth migration service (Jugendmigrationsdienst) (§ 14 SGB I).
If there is a dispute with the Jugendamt or the facility, an ombudsperson's office (Ombudsstelle) in your federal state can help. It works independently (§ 9a SGB VIII).
az.p.antrag: Write an application for help for young adults
az.p.antrag.t: A short letter is enough as an application. Here is a template.
az.p.kv.t:
Up to 25 you can be insured free of charge through your parents (Familienversicherung) if they have statutory insurance: always until 18, until 23 without work, until 25 at school, in training, studying or in voluntary service (§ 10 SGB V). If one parent is privately insured and earns much more, this is sometimes not possible. Ask the health insurance fund.
This ends when you are insured yourself – for example in paid training – or when you earn more than {grenze} a month (for a mini-job the mini-job limit applies). As a trainee, your employer registers you with the health insurance fund you choose.
az.p.phv.t: Pays if you accidentally damage something of someone else's. Otherwise this can be very expensive. You are often covered by your parents while at school or in your first training – check the conditions. At the latest after that you need your own.
az.p.bu: Occupational disability insurance (for everyone with income)
az.p.bu.t:
Pays if you can no longer work in your job due to illness or accident. Consumer advocates advise young people with income to take it out early.
It costs money every month. Before signing you must answer health questions honestly (§ 19 VVG). Previous illnesses can make the contract more expensive or prevent it. Compare and get independent advice.
az.p.kfzH: Motor liability insurance (only with a car)
az.p.kfzH.t: If you have a car or motorbike, it is compulsory. Without it, no vehicle is registered.
az.p.hausrat.t: Useful if you have your own valuable furniture or devices. If you have only rented a room, for example in a shared flat or a hall of residence, you may still be covered through your parents – ask first.
az.p.auslandKv.t: Consumer advocates recommend it for trips abroad in addition to your health insurance.
az.p.geraete.t: Often expensive compared with the benefit. Devices can usually be replaced.
az.p.restschuld: Payment protection insurance for a loan
az.p.restschuld.t: The Verbraucherzentrale does not consider it useful.
az.p.gepaeck.t: Usually unnecessary. Luggage is often already covered by household contents insurance.
